paper_title: Prometheus 2 An Open Source Language Model Specialized in Evaluating   Other Language Models
caption: When merging models, the influence of relative evaluation on absolute evaluation is greater than the influence of absolute evaluation on relative evaluation. Performance of Direct Assessment (colored in green) and Pairwise Ranking (colored in blue) when altering the value to merge evaluator LMs trained on different formats.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the performance of two evaluation methods—Direct Assessment Correlation (green line) and Pairwise Ranking Accuracy (blue line)—as a function of the merging ratio between evaluator language models trained on different formats, alongside a third metric, Average Performance (black line). The x-axis, labeled "(Direct Assessment : Pairwise Ranking) Merging Ratio," is linear and spans from 1.9 to 9.1, with tick marks at regular intervals of approximately 0.9. The y-axis on the left, labeled "Direct Assessment Pearson Correlation," ranges from 0.500 to 0.675 in linear increments, while the y-axis on the right, labeled "Pairwise Ranking Accuracy," ranges from 50 to 80, also in linear increments, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The green line, representing Direct Assessment Correlation, starts at 0.500 at a merging ratio of 1.9, rises steadily to a peak of 0.675 at 5.5, then declines to 0.600 at 6.4 before continuing its downward trend to 0.575 at 9.1. The blue line, representing Pairwise Ranking Accuracy, begins at approximately 0.670 at 1.9, peaks at 0.675 at 5.5, and then decreases sharply to 0.500 at 9.1. The black line, representing Average Performance, starts at 0.575 at 1.9, increases to a peak of 0.625 at 5.5, and then declines to 0.550 at 9.1. All three lines are plotted with solid lines and circular markers, with the green and blue lines showing similar trends but differing in magnitude and peak timing.
